# Oh Agent — full documentation (plain text)

Source: https://ohagent.ai/docs · Generated from the docs Markdown. Version described: 1.0.0-beta.2 (no public installer yet).

---

# What is Oh Agent? Open-source AI agent behavior analytics, with Agent City
URL: https://ohagent.ai/docs

Oh Agent is a free, open-source platform for analyzing your AI agents' behavior data. Agents are now part of everyday work and life, and Oh Agent's goal is to make them more valuable to you. It runs as a desktop app, built on the open-source **Agent Vitals** engine, with **Agent City** as its first app:

- **Agent Vitals**, the foundation: a local-first agent behavior data engine, embedded in the app (no server, no daemon). It reads the session history your agents (Claude Code, Codex and others) already keep on your machine, then parses and analyzes it: activity, tokens, cost estimates and behaviour findings.
- **Agent City**, built on Agent Vitals' data interface. It's an open-world data-visualization game where each session is a building in an explorable 3D city.

All analysis happens on your machine; your sessions are not uploaded.

## Key facts

- **Version:** 1.0.0-beta.2. A public installer is not available yet; [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/MixLabPro/oh-agent-ai/releases) has no download as of October 2026.
- **Platforms (first public release):** Apple Silicon Mac, Intel Mac, Windows and Linux installers. Apple Silicon macOS is the best-tested path; Intel / Windows / Linux are early / experimental while `SUPPORT_MATRIX.md` still does not declare them supported. See [Install](https://ohagent.ai/docs/install).
- **Supported agents:** Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek Harness and WorkBuddy.
- **One building = one session.** Building height follows the session's token count on a log curve.
- **Local-first:** no account and no API key needed; sessions are never uploaded.
- **License:** MIT. Source: [github.com/MixLabPro/oh-agent-ai](https://github.com/MixLabPro/oh-agent-ai).
- **Web demo:** [ohagent.ai](https://ohagent.ai/) runs the real City frontend on 2,000 synthetic sessions. It does not read your computer.

## What does Oh Agent show?

- **Agent City.** Each session becomes a data building, each agent gets its own district, and token volume shapes the skyline. Select a building to inspect its session. See [What each building means](https://ohagent.ai/docs/city-guide).
- **Activity replay.** Replay how the city grew within the selected time window (7, 30, 90 or 366 days on desktop).
- **Usage view.** A separate desktop view covers usage and cost by source and time. In the city, each building's details show an estimated cost, and public buildings such as City Hall open data panels.

The city is a picture of recorded activity, not a productivity score. A taller building means more tokens, not better work.

## Where does the data come from?

Oh Agent reads the session logs your agents already write to your home folder, for example `~/.claude/projects` for Claude Code and `~/.codex/sessions` for Codex. Details per agent:

- [Claude Code: where sessions are stored and how Oh Agent reads them](https://ohagent.ai/docs/data-sources/claude-code)
- [Codex: where sessions are stored and how Oh Agent reads them](https://ohagent.ai/docs/data-sources/codex)
- [DeepSeek Harness](https://ohagent.ai/docs/data-sources/deepseek-harness) · [WorkBuddy](https://ohagent.ai/docs/data-sources/workbuddy)
- Other agents: [extra folders and manifest sources](https://ohagent.ai/docs/integrations/custom-sources-and-manifests)

## How is it built, and can I extend it?

It's open source (MIT). See the [Agent Vitals engine](https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/overview) for its crates, CLI, MCP tools and App SDK, the [architecture overview](https://ohagent.ai/docs/architecture/overview) for how Agent Vitals and Agent City fit together, [Integrations](https://ohagent.ai/docs/integrations) for the local Data MCP server, plugins and exports, and [Add a data source](https://ohagent.ai/docs/contributing/adding-a-data-source) to contribute support for a new agent.

## Is my data private?

Yes. Sessions are analyzed on your machine and never uploaded. The app only goes online for a few public, data-free requests such as price tables and update checks. Full details: [Does Oh Agent upload my sessions?](https://ohagent.ai/docs/privacy-and-data) and the [privacy policy](https://ohagent.ai/privacy).

## How do I install it?

The public installer is still being prepared. See [Install](https://ohagent.ai/docs/install) for system requirements, which platforms the first release ships, and how developers can build it from source today.

## More

- [Agent City overview](https://ohagent.ai/city) · [Download](https://ohagent.ai/download) · [FAQ](https://ohagent.ai/faq)
- Brand note: the public name is **Oh Agent**. The desktop app is `Oh Agent.app`; the CLI and data folders still use the internal name `agent-vitals`, and you don't need to rename anything.

# What does each building in Agent City mean? How is height calculated?
URL: https://ohagent.ai/docs/city-guide

In Agent City, every session building stands for one agent session, and its height grows with that session's total token count on a logarithmic curve. Districts are agents (one per agent, such as Claude Code or Codex), and almost everything else (landmarks, beaches, traffic) is decoration that does not represent data.

## Key facts

- **1 session building = 1 session** within the selected time window.
- **Height = total tokens** (input + cache read + cache write + output) on a log curve, from **2.6** to **48** scene units.
- **1 district = 1 agent**; building colour = its district.
- **Up to 4,000** sessions per window are loaded, each as its own building (most recent first).
- **Facilities** (schools, malls, hospitals) appear about **once per 45 sessions**.
- The island grows **one tier per 400 sessions**, up to **10 tiers**.
- Desktop time windows: **7, 30, 90 or 366 days**.

## How is building height calculated?

Height comes only from the session's total tokens in the current window:

```
m      = max(0, log10(tokens) − 1)
height = clamp(0.75 × m^2.2, 2.6, 48)
```

| Tokens in the session | Height (scene units) |
|---|---|
| 575 or fewer | 2.6 (minimum) |
| 1,000 | 3.4 |
| 10,000 | 8.4 |
| 100,000 | 15.8 |
| 1,000,000 | 25.9 |
| 10,000,000 | 38.6 |
| about 42,000,000 or more | 48 (maximum) |

The log curve keeps the order (more tokens is always at least as tall) while keeping mid-sized sessions readable next to very large ones. Scene units are the city's internal scale. **TBD:** whether to present them as metres.

## Which tokens count?

The total includes uncached input, cache reads, cache writes and output tokens recorded for the session inside the selected window. Recorded tokens reflect what the agent logged on this Mac. They are not necessarily your complete history across devices.

## Why do buildings have different shapes?

Shape follows land value, not data. Session buildings on the district's most valuable lots (near the district centre, main roads and the water) grow into glass towers; on cheaper lots they become wide slabs or blocks. Low session buildings by the sea take a Miami Art Deco style, and a session on a seaside hotel lot becomes a hotel. In every case, **height still comes from tokens**.

## What do districts, landmarks and the city hall mean?

| Element | What it shows | Data? |
|---|---|---|
| District | One agent (harness), such as Claude Code or Codex; buildings take the district colour | Yes |
| District landmark | A stepped Art Deco tower at each district centre; it grows with the district's session count and rises floor by floor during replay | Yes (session count) |
| "Top of the city" | The session with the most tokens in the window wears a spire crown and, from dusk, a searchlight beam | Yes |
| City hall | Flags in front show each district's share of sessions; a beacon on the dome means a district has anomalies | Yes |
| Schools, malls, hospitals | City size: about one per 45 sessions; not any single session | Scale only |
| Island tier | The land expands one tier per 400 sessions, up to 10 tiers | Scale only |
| Backdrop towers | Muted skyline fill; can be turned off in City settings; not clickable, not counted | No |
| Seed landmarks (TV tower, lighthouse, Ferris wheel, pagoda…) | Chosen by the island seed | No |
| Beach, harbor, airport island, volcano, bridges, ring expressway | City scenery and skeleton | No |
| Cars, boats, pedestrians | Ambient animation | No |

## What happens with more than 4,000 sessions?

The desktop app loads at most 4,000 sessions per window, keeping the most recent ones by activity, and the city reports its coverage (sessions shown out of sessions found). Missing records are never filled in with invented activity. The City renderer can also merge sessions beyond its 4,000-building capacity into low-detail aggregated blocks; with the current 4,000 load limit this should not normally be reached. **TBD:** maintainer to confirm the wording of the coverage indicator.

## Is the city layout random?

No. The layout is generated from a seed plus the island tier, so the same seed and tier give the same city. The seed is stored locally in the app's data folder (`state/plugins/city.json`).

## Can I replay how the city grew?

Yes. The desktop app replays activity within the loaded window, with adjustable replay speed. The [web demo](https://ohagent.ai/) supports exploring buildings and replay on synthetic data, but it hides game, export and seed controls.

Photo and video export exist in the City frontend. **TBD:** whether they are enabled in the first public release.

## Does a taller city mean I worked better?

No. The city is a visual interpretation of recorded activity, not a productivity score. Building growth does not prove a task succeeded, and repetition alone does not prove wasted work. A building's details show an estimated cost, but cost never changes its height, and an estimate isn't a bill.

# Where does Claude Code store session history, and how does Oh Agent read it?
URL: https://ohagent.ai/docs/data-sources/claude-code

Claude Code saves each session as a JSON Lines file under `~/.claude/projects/`, one folder per project and one `.jsonl` file per session. Oh Agent reads those files on your Mac, without uploading them, and turns each session into a building in the Claude Code district of Agent City.

## Key facts

- **Location read:** `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` (all `.jsonl` files, recursively).
- **One file = one session.** The file name (without `.jsonl`) is the session ID.
- **Live updates:** Oh Agent watches `~/.claude/projects` and picks up new or growing sessions.
- **Tokens counted:** input, cache read, cache write and output tokens recorded in the log.
- **Read-only:** Oh Agent does not modify or move Claude Code's files.
- **Not followed yet:** a custom `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` location (see below). You can add extra folders in Settings → Additional read locations.

## Where exactly are Claude Code sessions stored?

On macOS the path is:

```
~/.claude/projects/<project-folder>/<session-id>.jsonl
```

Each line in the file is one event in the conversation (messages, tool calls, token usage). Claude Code creates `<project-folder>` from the directory you started it in.

## What does Oh Agent take from these files?

For each session Oh Agent records the time range, number of events and token counts, plus a short bounded title or task excerpt where available. Those feed the city: one building per session, with height from its total tokens. See [What each building means](https://ohagent.ai/docs/city-guide).

The Agent City view never receives full prompts, file paths, working directories, tool arguments or raw errors. Raw conversation text stays in Claude Code's own files. See [Does Oh Agent upload my sessions?](https://ohagent.ai/docs/privacy-and-data).

## Why is my Claude Code district empty or smaller than expected?

- **No sessions yet in the window.** The desktop city shows the last 7, 30, 90 or 366 days; widen the window.
- **Old transcripts were cleaned up.** Oh Agent can only show sessions whose log files still exist on this Mac. By default Claude Code deletes transcripts after 30 days; see [Why are my older sessions missing?](#why-are-my-older-sessions-missing-from-agent-city)
- **Another device.** History from other computers isn't merged.
- **Custom config folder.** If you set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, Claude Code stores session history there instead of `~/.claude` (per [Anthropic's settings docs](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/settings)). Oh Agent 1.0.0-beta.2 doesn't follow that variable. You can add extra folders in Settings, but they are read as `<folder>/.claude/projects`, so they don't cover most custom config folders. **TBD:** confirm this behaviour; see [Extra folders and manifest sources](https://ohagent.ai/docs/integrations/custom-sources-and-manifests).
- **More than 4,000 sessions.** The most recent 4,000 sessions in the window are loaded.
- **Permission.** macOS may ask you to allow Oh Agent to read the folder.

## Why are my older sessions missing from Agent City?

Claude Code deletes old session transcripts by itself. Its `cleanupPeriodDays` setting defaults to **30 days**, and the cleanup runs quietly in the background after a session starts. Oh Agent can only import sessions whose log files are still on your Mac. So if Claude Code removed a transcript before Oh Agent ever read it, that session can't appear in Agent City, even in the 90- or 366-day window.

To keep more history, raise the value in `~/.claude/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "cleanupPeriodDays": 365
}
```

The value is a whole number of days, at least 1. `0` is rejected; for very long retention, Anthropic suggests a large value such as `3650`. The setting only affects transcripts that still exist. It can't bring back deleted ones.

Sessions Oh Agent has already imported stay in its own database after Claude Code deletes the log file. They are removed by Oh Agent's own retention (13 months by default) or when you delete a source's data in Settings. **TBD:** confirm on a real install that already-imported sessions still appear in the City after their log file is gone.

## Do I need an API key or to be logged in?

No. Oh Agent reads files Claude Code already wrote. It needs no Anthropic API key and no Oh Agent account.

# Where does Codex store session logs, and how does Oh Agent visualize them?
URL: https://ohagent.ai/docs/data-sources/codex

Codex saves each session as a "rollout" file, `rollout-*.jsonl`, under `~/.codex/sessions/` (organised by date), and archived sessions under `~/.codex/archived_sessions/`. Oh Agent reads both folders on your Mac, without uploading anything, and shows each session as a building in the Codex district of Agent City.

## Key facts

- **Locations read:** `~/.codex/sessions/` and `~/.codex/archived_sessions/`, recursively.
- **Files read:** only names matching `rollout-*.jsonl`.
- **One rollout file = one session.**
- **Archived sessions count too**, so archiving in Codex doesn't remove them from the city.
- **Live updates:** Oh Agent watches `~/.codex` for changes.
- **Not followed yet:** a custom `CODEX_HOME` location (see below). You can add extra folders in Settings → Additional read locations.

## Where exactly are Codex sessions stored?

A typical path looks like this:

```
~/.codex/sessions/2026/08/22/rollout-2026-08-22T22-06-31-<id>.jsonl
```

Sessions are grouped into year/month/day folders, and the file name starts with the session's start time. Each line is one event (messages, tool calls, token counts).

## What does Oh Agent take from these files?

The same per-session summary as for other agents: time range, event count, token counts (input, cache read, cache write, output) and a short bounded title or task excerpt where available. Height in the city comes from total tokens. See [What each building means](https://ohagent.ai/docs/city-guide).

File paths, working directories, tool arguments and raw errors are never passed to the City view. Details: [Does Oh Agent upload my sessions?](https://ohagent.ai/docs/privacy-and-data).

## Why are some Codex sessions missing?

- **Outside the time window.** Widen it to 30, 90 or 366 days.
- **Custom `CODEX_HOME`.** Codex can keep its data in another folder via the `CODEX_HOME` environment variable (**TBD:** link OpenAI's Codex docs). Oh Agent 1.0.0-beta.2 doesn't follow that variable. You can add extra folders in Settings, but they are read as `<folder>/.codex/sessions` and `<folder>/.codex/archived_sessions`. **TBD:** confirm this behaviour; see [Extra folders and manifest sources](https://ohagent.ai/docs/integrations/custom-sources-and-manifests).
- **Deleted log files.** Sessions whose rollout files were removed can't be shown; Oh Agent never invents missing activity.
- **Other devices.** History from other computers isn't merged.
- **More than 4,000 sessions.** The most recent 4,000 in the window are loaded.

## Does Oh Agent need my OpenAI API key?

No. It reads the files Codex already saved. No API key and no Oh Agent account are needed.

## Related

- [See your Codex history as a 3D city](https://ohagent.ai/codex)

# Where does DeepSeek Harness (DSH) store sessions, and how does Oh Agent read them?
URL: https://ohagent.ai/docs/data-sources/deepseek-harness

DeepSeek Harness (DSH) keeps each session as a `session.jsonl` file, sometimes compressed as `session.jsonl.zstd`, under the `sessions/` folder of its home directory. That directory is `$DSH_HOME`, or `~/.dsh` if the variable isn't set. Agent Vitals reads these files on your Mac and shows each session as a building in the DSH district of Agent City.

## Key facts

- **Location:** `$DSH_HOME/sessions/`, recursively. `DSH_HOME` defaults to `~/.dsh`.
- **Files read:** `session.jsonl` and `session.jsonl.zstd`.
- **`DSH_HOME` is followed**, even outside your home folder. This is the only built-in source that honours an environment variable for its location.
- **Titles** come from DSH's workspace index, `storages/workspace.json`.
- **Behaviour checks:** yes. DSH sessions get the same SV6xx findings as Claude Code and Codex.
- **Extra folders:** supported in Settings.

## What does Oh Agent take from DSH sessions?

The same summary as for other sources: time range, event count, token counts and a bounded title. DSH logs record provider evidence, so cost estimates for DSH can tell routes apart better than for Claude Code.

## Is there also a DSH plugin?

Yes, but it's separate from session reading. The `dsh-agent-vitals` bundle in `integrations/dsh/` adds the older skill auditor as a skill inside DSH (`dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-agent-vitals`). You don't need it for Agent City.

**TBD:** link to DeepSeek Harness's official docs, and confirm the display name City uses for this district ("DSH" in the fixtures).

- [Integrations overview](https://ohagent.ai/docs/integrations)

# How does Oh Agent read WorkBuddy sessions?
URL: https://ohagent.ai/docs/data-sources/workbuddy

For WorkBuddy, Agent Vitals reads usage from the `trace_*.json` files under `~/.workbuddy/traces/`, on your Mac. Each WorkBuddy session becomes a building in the WorkBuddy district of Agent City. WorkBuddy support is narrower than for the other built-in sources: you can't add extra folders, behaviour checks don't run during sync, and sessions don't get titles yet.

## Key facts

- **Location:** `~/.workbuddy/` (fixed; no environment variable).
- **Usage files:** `trace_*.json` under `~/.workbuddy/traces/`.
- **Session audit** (CLI `workbuddy-session`) also reads `workbuddy.db` (`sessions`, `session_usage`) and `audit-log/*.jsonl`.
- **Extra folders:** not supported.
- **Behaviour findings:** none during normal sync.
- **Titles:** not yet. They live in `workbuddy.db`, which isn't wired up for titles.

## How are WorkBuddy costs shown?

WorkBuddy bills in its own credits. Oh Agent reports credits as credits, not money. A nominal yuan value (credits × 0.05, based on the public top-up price) appears only in the nominal column, never as money actually paid, and the cash-paid field stays empty because there's no payment evidence on your Mac.

**TBD:** link to WorkBuddy's official site and confirm which WorkBuddy versions write `traces/`.

- [DeepSeek Harness data source](https://ohagent.ai/docs/data-sources/deepseek-harness)

# Does Oh Agent upload my sessions? Data and privacy explained
URL: https://ohagent.ai/docs/privacy-and-data

No. Oh Agent analyzes your agent history on your Mac and never uploads sessions, logs or analysis results. This page explains exactly what the app reads, the few times it goes online, and where the boundaries change (MCP and export). For the legal policy, see the [privacy policy](https://ohagent.ai/privacy).

## Key facts

- Sessions are analyzed locally. **No upload, no telemetry, no cloud sync.**
- **No account and no API key** needed.
- Network requests are limited to public files (price tables, exchange rates, release check, optional official plugin index) and **carry no local data**.
- The City view gets a bounded per-session summary. It **never sees file paths, working directories, tool arguments, raw errors or full prompts**.
- Raw conversation text stays in your agents' own log files; Oh Agent's database stores pointers and statistics, not full copies.
- MIT-licensed source you can inspect. Open source is not a security certification.

## Does Oh Agent upload my sessions?

No. Oh Agent analyzes your agent history on your Mac and never uploads sessions, logs or analysis results. No cloud account and no API key are required.

Analysis results stay in a local database on your Mac. The [web demo](https://ohagent.ai/) uses synthetic sessions only and does not read anything from your computer.

## What files does Oh Agent read?

Oh Agent reads the session logs that supported agents already keep in your home folder: ~/.claude/projects for Claude Code, ~/.codex/sessions and ~/.codex/archived_sessions for Codex, ~/.workbuddy for WorkBuddy, and ~/.dsh (or $DSH_HOME) for DeepSeek Harness.

| Agent | Folder read | Details |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` | [Claude Code data source](https://ohagent.ai/docs/data-sources/claude-code) |
| Codex | `~/.codex/sessions`, `~/.codex/archived_sessions` (`rollout-*.jsonl`) | [Codex data source](https://ohagent.ai/docs/data-sources/codex) |
| WorkBuddy | `~/.workbuddy` | — |
| DeepSeek Harness | `~/.dsh`, or `$DSH_HOME` if set | — |

Raw conversation text stays in those files. Oh Agent's own database keeps pointers into the logs (source and event IDs, offsets) plus derived statistics, not a full copy. If an agent deletes or rotates an old log, Oh Agent says the source has expired instead of keeping its own copy.

macOS may ask you to allow access to these folders. **TBD:** the exact permission prompt in the first public release.

## When does the Oh Agent app use the network?

Only for a few public requests that carry no local data: downloading public price and exchange-rate tables, checking for a new release on GitHub, and, if you choose to, downloading the official plugin index or signed packages.

| Request | Destination | What is sent |
|---|---|---|
| Price table and exchange-rate snapshot (checked about every 6 hours, behind an update switch) | Static JSON files on `raw.githubusercontent.com` in the project repository | A plain file download, no user data |
| New-version check | GitHub Releases API for the project repository | A plain request, no user data |
| Official plugin index or signed packages (only when you opt in) | Fixed public HTTPS sources | A plain download, no user data |

No request may include local logs, machine identifiers, credentials or analysis data. **TBD:** whether the price-table update switch is on by default.

## What can the Agent City view see?

The City receives only declared, bounded fields. Per session: an opaque ID, the agent, start and end time, event count, token counts split into uncached input, cache read, cache write and output, the model IDs used, an estimated cost with its status, a short bounded title and up to two short task excerpts, and a stable City asset ID. For the whole window: totals, daily activity, findings counted per agent and severity, and recorded skill use (skill name, invocation count, outcomes, last use). It cannot see full prompts, raw logs, file paths, working directories, tool arguments or raw error messages.

Session IDs given to the City are salted, app-specific identifiers, not the agent's own session IDs. The City runs as a built-in plugin: it never touches the database or log files directly, cannot run arbitrary SQL, and only receives the fields the host declares for it. Cost figures are estimates, not bills. The City asset ID is random and kept in a separate local registry; it isn't derived from your files.

## Does connecting Oh Agent to an AI agent over MCP change privacy?

Yes. MCP serves redacted data to agents running on your Mac, but if that agent talks to a cloud model, whatever it receives can leave your machine inside its context. Connecting an agent is your decision and is not the same as viewing data locally.

The built-in MCP server keeps its redaction rules: it never exposes raw errors or tool-call arguments. Exports are redacted by default; a private export has to be chosen explicitly.

## Does Oh Agent store my API keys?

No. Credentials are never saved in anything Oh Agent owns. Some test features can pass a key to a child process in memory only.

## Does the ohagent.ai website use analytics?

**TBD (choose one before publishing):**

- **Option A (keep Cloudflare Web Analytics):** "The ohagent.ai website uses Cloudflare Web Analytics to count page visits. It does not set cookies (**TBD:** confirm against Cloudflare's documentation). This applies to the website only; the Oh Agent app has no analytics."
- **Option B (no website analytics):** "The ohagent.ai website does not use analytics." (Only true after automatic Web Analytics injection is turned off for ohagent.ai in Cloudflare.)

# How do I install Oh Agent? System requirements and release status
URL: https://ohagent.ai/docs/install

You can't download a ready-made Oh Agent installer yet: version 1.0.0-beta.2 is in release preparation, and the [GitHub Releases page](https://github.com/MixLabPro/oh-agent-ai/releases) has no installer so far. The **first public release** is planned to publish installers for **Apple Silicon Mac, Intel Mac, Windows and Linux**. Apple Silicon macOS is the best-tested path today; the other platforms ship as early / experimental builds. Developers can already build the app from source.

**Release status:** As of October 2026 there is **no public, signed installer**. Any build you make yourself is a local developer build. It is not Developer ID–signed or notarized (macOS). **TBD:** update this page on release day with download links and per-platform install steps.

## Key facts

- **Current version:** 1.0.0-beta.2 (not yet released publicly).
- **First public release ships installers for:** Apple Silicon Mac, Intel Mac, Windows (x64), and Linux (x64).
- **macOS:** 11.0 or later (`minimumSystemVersion` in `tauri.conf.json`).
- **Apple Silicon (arm64):** best-tested path; SUPPORT_MATRIX status is "release candidate in validation".
- **Intel Mac (x86_64), Windows, Linux:** installers are published by the release workflow, but SUPPORT_MATRIX still does **not** declare them supported. Treat them as **early / experimental**. **TBD:** which bugs are known on each platform; update after real-machine acceptance.
- **Price:** free and open source (MIT).
- **Checksums:** every release includes a `SHA256SUMS` file next to the installers.

## What files will the first release publish?

Public names come from the release workflow (version = app version without the `app-v` tag prefix, must match `tauri.conf.json`):

| Platform | Public artifact name |
| --- | --- |
| macOS Apple Silicon | `Oh-Agent-<version>-macos-arm64.dmg` and `Oh-Agent-<version>-macos-arm64.app.zip` |
| macOS Intel | `Oh-Agent-<version>-macos-x64.dmg` and `Oh-Agent-<version>-macos-x64.app.zip` |
| Windows x64 | `Oh-Agent-<version>-windows-x64-setup.exe` |
| Linux x64 | `Oh-Agent-<version>-linux-x64.deb` and `Oh-Agent-<version>-linux-x64.AppImage` |
| All | `SHA256SUMS` |

On macOS the installed app is `Oh Agent.app` (bundle identifier `ai.ohagent.desktop`). On Windows the NSIS installer is verified in CI to start with the display name `Oh Agent`; on Linux the `.desktop` entry is `Name=Oh Agent`. The bundled CLI binary stays named `agent-vitals` / `agent-vitals.exe`.

## Platform maturity (important)

`apps/desktop/src-tauri/SUPPORT_MATRIX.md` only records combinations that have build **and** acceptance evidence. As of the docs worktree (`bf7196a`):

- **macOS 11+ / Apple Silicon (`arm64`):** "候选验证中" — local `.app` and bundled CLI are arm64; architecture preflight, CLI `--version` and Vite/Workbench checks passed. Formal release still requires Developer ID, notarization, clean-machine install / upgrade / restore, and resource/performance acceptance.
- **macOS 11+ / Intel (`x86_64`):** matrix says **未支持** ("尚无本机或 CI 产物证据"). The release workflow **does** build and publish `macos-x64` artifacts on a `macos-15-intel` runner, so the matrix text is behind the CI. Until the matrix is updated and real-machine acceptance is done, docs call Intel **early / experimental**. **TBD:** known Intel bugs.
- **Windows / Linux:** matrix explicitly does **not** declare a desktop release. The `desktop-platforms.yml` workflow builds and CI-tests NSIS / deb / AppImage packages, and `release-desktop.yml` uploads them. Docs call these **early / experimental**. **TBD:** known Windows and Linux bugs; OS version floors beyond what Tauri needs.

No universal macOS binary is declared.

## When will the installer be available?

**TBD.** The first public installers will be published once signing (macOS Developer ID + notarization), packaging and the planned clean-machine checks pass for the platforms you care about. To get notified:

- Watch releases on [GitHub](https://github.com/MixLabPro/oh-agent-ai) (Watch → Custom → Releases).
- Follow [@ohagentai](https://x.com/ohagentai) on X.
- Check the [download page](https://ohagent.ai/download).

## How will installing work once it's released?

From the Releases page, download the artifact that matches your OS and CPU, then verify it against `SHA256SUMS`. The app bundles its own `agent-vitals` command-line tool, so you won't need Python, a separate CLI or any `PATH` changes (documented for the macOS bundle; **TBD** confirm the same story on Windows and Linux installers beyond the CI smoke tests). **TBD:** exact step-by-step instructions and screenshots per platform, written against the real release packages.

## Can I try Oh Agent without installing?

Yes, partly. The [web demo on ohagent.ai](https://ohagent.ai/) runs the real City frontend on 2,000 synthetic sessions (30-day window). It doesn't read your logs, and it hides the game, export and seed controls.

## How can developers build Oh Agent from source today?

The repository documents a local **macOS** build most clearly. You need a recent Node.js with npm, stable Rust, Tauri's platform prerequisites and the Tauri CLI. From the repository root:

```sh
# Command-line tool
cargo build --release
./target/release/agent-vitals --help

# Local macOS .app build
npm ci --prefix apps/desktop/ui-dev
npm ci --prefix apps/agent-city/ui
bash scripts/build-macos-react-app.sh

# Launch the bundle (not the bare menubar executable)
open "apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/macos/Oh Agent.app"
```

This produces a locally signed test build for development only. See the [desktop README](https://github.com/MixLabPro/oh-agent-ai/blob/dev/apps/desktop/src-tauri/README.md) for details. **TBD:** document Windows and Linux local build steps the same way (CI already runs `cargo tauri build` with `nsis` / `deb,appimage` bundles).

## Why do I still see agent-vitals after installing?

The app display name is Oh Agent. The bundled command-line tool, some internal paths and the data folder `~/.agent-vitals/` (macOS/Linux) still use the earlier name `agent-vitals`. Don't rename them. Your data isn't tied to the app identifier, so it stays where it is.

If you ran a pre-release macOS build named `agent-vitals.app` (identifier `com.mixlabpro.agent-vitals`), quit and delete it. Otherwise macOS shows two menu bar icons. **TBD:** upgrading from the old bundle hasn't been tested on a real Mac; **TBD:** Windows/Linux upgrade paths from any older package name.

## What happens after I open it?

Oh Agent reads your agents' existing logs. You need no account and no API key. The OS may ask permission to read those folders. Next:

- [Claude Code data source](https://ohagent.ai/docs/data-sources/claude-code) · [Codex data source](https://ohagent.ai/docs/data-sources/codex)
- [What each building in Agent City means](https://ohagent.ai/docs/city-guide)
- [Does Oh Agent upload my sessions?](https://ohagent.ai/docs/privacy-and-data)
- [FAQ](https://ohagent.ai/faq)

# What is the Agent Vitals engine? Local-first agent behavior data engine
URL: https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/overview

Oh Agent is built on the open-source **Agent Vitals** engine, and Agent City is its first app. Agent Vitals is a local-first engine for AI agent behavior data. It reads the session logs that Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek Harness and WorkBuddy already write, turns them into usage facts and behaviour findings, stores them in an embedded SQLite database, and serves them through read-only interfaces: a CLI, a stdio MCP server, and projections for apps. It's a set of Rust libraries linked into the desktop app and the CLI, not a server: it opens no network port and runs no daemon.

## Key facts

- **Embedded, not a service:** the data layer is described in code as "an embedded local data layer, not a standalone service: no network port, no daemon."
- **One store:** `agent-vitals.sqlite3` in `~/.agent-vitals/` (or `AGENT_VITALS_HOME`). It doesn't repair itself; a corrupted file is rebuilt with `data-migrate`.
- **Who runs it:** the desktop app links the crates and syncs every 5 minutes in-process. The `agent-vitals` CLI runs the same code on demand.
- **Interfaces out:** the [CLI](https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/cli), the [Data MCP tools](https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/mcp-tools) (stdio only), the [App SDK](https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/app-sdk) projections, and JSONL exports.
- **Two implementations:** Rust is the product; a [Python twin](https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/python) is kept byte-identical through golden tests.
- **Name:** "Agent Vitals" was the project's earlier name, so crates, the CLI and data folders are still called `agent-vitals`.

## How do the crates fit together?

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  SRC["Agent logs on disk<br/>~/.claude · ~/.codex · ~/.dsh · ~/.workbuddy · harnesses.d"]
  H["agent-vitals-harnesses<br/>(claude_code, codex, dsh, workbuddy, openclaw, generic)"]
  I["agent-vitals-ingest (L5)<br/>sync · tick · watcher · findings"]
  D[("agent-vitals-data<br/>agent-vitals.sqlite3")]
  Q["agent-vitals-query (L2–L3)<br/>sources · sessions · projections"]
  B["agent-vitals-billing (L4)"]
  T["agent-vitals-trust (L5)"]
  M["agent-vitals-mcp (L6)"]
  R["agent-vitals-runtime<br/>(facade, re-exports all)"]
  DESK["Desktop app (Tauri 2)"]
  CLI["agent-vitals CLI"]
  PH["Plugin host"]
  SDK["@agent-vitals/app-sdk"]
  CITY["Agent City"]
  DOM["agent-vitals-domain + vitals-core<br/>(pure rules)"]
  W["agent-vitals-wasm"]
  SRC --> H --> I --> D --> Q
  Q --> B & T & M
  B & T & M --> R
  I --> R
  R --> DESK & CLI
  DESK --> PH --> SDK --> CITY
  DOM --> H
  DOM --> W
```

In words: agent logs → `agent-vitals-harnesses` parsers → `agent-vitals-ingest` sync → `agent-vitals-data` SQLite store → `agent-vitals-query` read layer → billing, trust and MCP on top → the `agent-vitals-runtime` facade → the desktop app and CLI. In the desktop app, the plugin host passes projections through the App SDK to Agent City. The pure rules in `agent-vitals-domain` and `vitals-core` are shared by everything, including the wasm build.

## What does each crate do?

| Layer | Crate | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pure | `vitals-core` | Harness-agnostic behavioural audit engine (events, signals, detectors, findings). The SV601–SV614 rules run here |
| Pure | `agent-vitals-domain` | Shared vocabulary (usage fact, source identity, harness capability) and cross-agent calculations (behaviour, cost, usage) |
| Pure | `agent-vitals-provider` | Provider identity and attribution. No I/O, SQL or network |
| Adapters | `agent-vitals-harnesses` | Per-agent log parsing and the session source registry; file I/O sits behind the `sources` feature |
| Store | `agent-vitals-data` | The SQLite authority store: schema, migrations, transactions, the single fact writer, typed repository |
| L0–L1 | `agent-vitals-runtime-core` | Data folder, clock, leases, state, pricing, tool-response envelope, events outbox |
| L2–L3 | `agent-vitals-query` | Source config, manifest registry, watch topology, summaries, traces, exports, app projections |
| L4 | `agent-vitals-billing` | Budgets, billing preview and attribution, price discovery, quota reminders |
| L5 | `agent-vitals-ingest` | Sync service, in-process engine, tick scheduler, watcher, findings evaluation, manifest install |
| L5 | `agent-vitals-trust` | Local trust / egress history audit |
| L6 | `agent-vitals-mcp` | Data MCP tool layer, the outbound face where redaction is reviewed |
| Facade | `agent-vitals-runtime` | No code of its own; re-exports the layers so `agent_vitals_runtime::X` paths stay stable |
| Tooling | `agent-vitals-probe` | Runner for the desktop "Test" tab (identity probes; credentials passed in memory only) |
| Browser | `agent-vitals-wasm` | wasm-bindgen wrapper: pure behaviour audit and cost folding on events already in memory. Built with wasm-pack, not part of the default build |

Layering is enforced: crates may only depend on strictly lower layers (Cargo), and `tests/module_layering.rs` checks modules inside the runtime family.

**TBD:** who ships the wasm build today. Its doc mentions a DSH audit tab, but no CI workflow or script in the repo builds it.

## What does Agent Vitals refuse to do?

- **Upload user data.** No telemetry, crash reports with payloads, or cloud sync without an explicit, reviewed product decision.
- **Store credentials.** API keys and tokens are never written to anything it owns.
- **Copy transcripts.** It stores anchors and derived fields; full text stays in the agents' logs.
- **Guess costs.** Unproven routes stay `metered_estimate` with `has_unresolved`.

- [Data pipeline](https://ohagent.ai/docs/architecture/data-pipeline)
- [CLI](https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/cli) · [Data MCP tools](https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/mcp-tools) · [App SDK](https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/app-sdk) · [Python twin](https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/python)

# Agent Vitals CLI (agent-vitals): commands for syncing, querying and exporting agent data
URL: https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/cli

`agent-vitals` is the command-line front end of the Agent Vitals engine. It runs the same Rust code as the desktop app: sync agent logs into the local database, check data status, export facts, manage manifest sources, audit single sessions, and start the [Data MCP server](https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/mcp-tools). It also keeps the commands of the earlier skill auditor. Help text is in English, and most commands take `--json`.

## Key facts

- **Source:** `apps/cli/` (subcommands in `apps/cli/src/main.rs`, built with clap).
- **Build:** `cargo build --release`, which gives `./target/release/agent-vitals`. Run `agent-vitals --help` for the full list.
- **Bundled:** the desktop app includes the binary as `bin/agent-vitals`.
- **Same data folder** as the app: `~/.agent-vitals/` or `AGENT_VITALS_HOME`.

## Data commands (the engine)

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `sync-facts` | Routine sync: find logs, diff, parse, write to the SQL store. Safe to re-run |
| `data-status` | Store status: schema version, recent sync runs, source counts, data-quality summary |
| `data …` | Read-only summaries (for example `data coverage`, `data daily`) |
| `data-export-private --out DIR` | Export facts with identities as stored, one `<harness>.jsonl` per source |
| `data-export-redacted --out DIR` | Same export with identity fields replaced by stable pseudonyms |
| `data-unresolved` | Drill into unpriced or unresolved usage per model for a month |
| `billing-groups`, `data-harness-bill` | Billing confirmation groups; user-entered harness bills |
| `budget`, `budget-sql` | Budget alert status and management |
| `data-migrate` | One-time import of legacy facts JSONL into the SQL store |
| `data-reimport-verify` | Re-import into two throwaway databases and compare (doesn't touch your store) |
| `sessions …` | Versioned read-only session queries |
| `routes-quality` | Passive report of recorded model identity by source and model family |
| `data-mcp serve [--allow-local-writes]` | Start the stdio [Data MCP server](https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/mcp-tools) |

**TBD:** the `sync-facts` help text still says "across all three harnesses", but the registry has four sources (WorkBuddy was added). Fix the help text or confirm.

## Source commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `harness-inventory --window-days 30` | Which sources are registered, have data, or are only candidates. Never activates anything |
| `harnesses` | Print the declared capabilities of the four built-in sources |
| `manifest-validate`, `manifest-install`, `manifest-list`, `manifest-uninstall`, `manifest-rollback`, `manifest-recompute`, `manifest-catalog-status` | [Manifest sources](https://ohagent.ai/docs/integrations/custom-sources-and-manifests): dry-run, preview → confirm, list, remove, roll back |
| `claude-usage-facts`, `codex-usage-facts`, `dsh-usage-facts`, `workbuddy-usage-facts` | Parse one source's files into usage-fact rows, for diagnosis |

## Session audit and trace commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `claude-session`, `codex-session`, `workbuddy-session`, `codex-evidence` | Audit one session into a normalized session with coverage and SV601–SV614 findings |
| `behavior`, `skill-audit`, `duration-audit` | Audit a DSH session log for risky behaviour, skill use or durations |
| `trace-ref` | Build the trace graph for a session from `sessions list`, without exposing file paths |
| `trace`, `trace-anchors` | Trace graph for one file; anchor report for local viewing only (never an MCP tool) |
| `codex-cost` | Price Codex token usage per model and day |
| `probe`, `trust …` | Desktop "Test" tab probes; local trust / egress history audit |

## Older skill-auditor commands

`list`, `doctor`, `plan`, `snapshot`, `diff`, `explain` and `overlap` come from the earlier skill auditor: they list installed Agent Skills, diagnose why one doesn't load, and plan cleanup. They are kept but aren't the main product story. See [Skill auditor](https://ohagent.ai/docs/integrations/skill-auditor).

## Examples

```sh
# Import new sessions now instead of waiting for the app's 5-minute sync
agent-vitals sync-facts

# Is the data fresh?
agent-vitals data-status --json

# Back up your facts, pseudonymized
agent-vitals data-export-redacted --out ~/oh-agent-export
```

**TBD:** test these exact invocations on a real install. Flags like `--json` vary per command; check `agent-vitals <command> --help`.

- [Data MCP tools](https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/mcp-tools)
- [Python twin](https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/python)

# Agent Vitals Data MCP tools: let your AI agent read your agent data locally
URL: https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/mcp-tools

Agent Vitals, the data layer of Oh Agent, has a local MCP server. Run `agent-vitals data-mcp serve`, register it in an MCP client such as Claude Code or Codex, and that agent can ask typed questions about your usage: data status, hourly usage, sessions, cost breakdowns, data-quality issues. It talks over stdio only, opens the database read-only, and can only change settings if you start it with `--allow-local-writes`.

## Key facts

- **Command:** `agent-vitals data-mcp serve`. The server name is `agent-vitals-data`.
- **Transport:** stdio, JSON-RPC 2.0, one JSON message per line. MCP protocol version `2025-06-18`.
- **Methods:** `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `ping`. No resources or prompts.
- **Read-only by default.** It opens the database read-only and never creates or migrates it.
- **Writes need a flag.** `--allow-local-writes` turns on typed settings and billing actions. There is still no arbitrary SQL, URL fetching or general file writing.
- **No network listener.** It only runs while a client keeps its stdin open.

## Which tools are available?

| Tool | What it answers |
| --- | --- |
| `data_status` | Is the data fresh? Coverage per source, last sync |
| `usage_hourly` | Token usage by hour and source |
| `sessions_search` / `session_detail` / `session_trace` | Find sessions and inspect a redacted session summary or trace |
| `cost_breakdown` | Estimated cost by price version, currency and billing basis, with unresolved usage shown separately |
| `budget_profiles` | Budget settings and status |
| `price_cards` | Models missing a price card; with `--allow-local-writes`, your agent can add user-set price cards |
| `data_quality_issues` | Data-quality problems, filtered, with redacted details |
| `issues_summary` / `skills_summary` | Behaviour findings and skill-usage summaries |
| `control_plane` | Source status, extra folders, exclusions, retention, time zone, sync pause/run, catalog policy (writes need the flag) |
| `trust_profile_*` | Schema, list, validate, stage and status for Trust audit profiles |

Three more tools (`query_sql_readonly`, `billing_workflow`, `authority_audit`) are only compiled in with the internal `mcp-internal` feature, so they aren't in normal builds.

## How do I connect it to Claude Code or Codex?

Point your MCP client at the `agent-vitals` binary with the arguments `data-mcp serve`. A generic MCP client entry looks like this:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "oh-agent": {
      "command": "/path/to/agent-vitals",
      "args": ["data-mcp", "serve"]
    }
  }
}
```

**TBD:** the binary's exact path inside the installed app. The bundle places it as a resource at `bin/agent-vitals`, which on macOS is likely `/Applications/Oh Agent.app/Contents/Resources/bin/agent-vitals` (note the space in the app name; quote the path). Verify on a real install. A developer build is at `target/release/agent-vitals`.

**TBD:** tested, copy-paste setup steps for Claude Code (`claude mcp add …`) and Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`). The repo doesn't document client setup.

## What does the MCP server never reveal?

- Raw error text and tool-call arguments, which are redacted in issue summaries.
- Native session IDs. Sessions are referred to by keyed one-way references.
- Absolute file paths, which `control_plane` reads never return.
- Credentials and confidential probe tasks.

Keep in mind that whatever the server returns lands in your agent's context, and that agent may send it to its model provider. Connecting MCP isn't the same as viewing data locally in the app.

The repo treats this as an egress boundary. `crates/agent-vitals-mcp` is the outbound face where the redaction rules are reviewed, and the stdio transport lives separately in `apps/cli/src/mcp.rs`. Redaction is applied when data is served, never by dropping data at ingest.

## Does the MCP server let my agent edit the city?

No. No current tool edits Agent City or its map. Letting agents help build the city is a planned idea; see the [Roadmap](https://ohagent.ai/docs/integrations#roadmap--规划中).

- [Agent Vitals engine overview](https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/overview) · [CLI](https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/cli)
- [Integrations overview](https://ohagent.ai/docs/integrations)
- [Does Oh Agent upload my sessions?](https://ohagent.ai/docs/privacy-and-data)
- [Architecture overview](https://ohagent.ai/docs/architecture/overview)

# Agent Vitals App SDK: how Agent City and other plugins read Vitals data
URL: https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/app-sdk

Agent City is the first app built on the Agent Vitals engine, and it runs as a plugin of the Oh Agent desktop app. A plugin is a web frontend that runs in its own WebView inside the app window and asks the host for data through one message type, `plugin_request`. The host checks the plugin's declared permissions in `apps/desktop/plugins.json`, runs the query in Rust, and returns only that projection. Today plugins are official and compiled into the app. You add one by contributing to the repo, not by installing a package.

## Key facts

- **Registry:** `apps/desktop/plugins.json`. City is the only entry today; it declares `city:v2`, `city:v3`, `city-settings:v1` and `harnesses:v1`.
- **Isolation:** each plugin runs in a separate WebView in the same window (an iframe in the browser preview), and only one plugin is active at a time.
- **Permissions:** `dataProjections` lists what a plugin may read. The default is nothing.
- **No database access:** plugins never get SQL, file paths, raw logs or unrestricted host IPC.
- **Shared SDK:** `packages/agent-vitals-app-sdk/` (`@agent-vitals/app-sdk`) holds the protocol types and the UI transport.
- **Compiled in:** the registry is embedded at build time, so changing it means rebuilding the app.

## What is in the SDK?

`@agent-vitals/app-sdk` (private, version `0.0.0`, not published to npm) exports:

| Export | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `PluginRequestV1` | `{version: 1, instanceId, requestId, method, payload}`, the only request envelope from plugin to host |
| `PluginResponseV1` | `{version: 1, requestId, ok, result, error: {code, retryable}}` |
| `PluginState*` types | A bounded private JSON store per plugin: up to 32 KiB per document, with revision-based optimistic writes |
| `CityUiProjectionV2` | The `city:v2` payload Agent City renders by default |
| `CityProjectionV3`, `CitySnapshotV3`, `CityWindowV3`, `CitySessionV3`, `CityModuleV3` | The paged `city:v3` types: snapshot context, half-open window, session rows with `asset_ref`, and module states (`ready`, `empty`, `unsupported`, `unavailable`, `stale`) |
| `validateCityProjectionV2`, `validateCityProjectionV3` | Runtime validators City runs on every response: safe integers, token sums, at most 4,000 (v2) or 500 per page (v3) sessions, `sr_` snapshot handles |
| `HarnessPublicIdentityV1`, `HarnessListV1`, `HarnessSessionsV1` | The generic `harnesses:v1` types |
| `createHarnessDataClient(instanceId, send)` | A helper for `list`, `sessions` and a consistent `snapshot` |
| `negotiateProjection` | Picks a projection version both sides support |
| `./ui-host` | Toolbar publishing, host commands, locale and health signals for the embedded page |

Contract types are generated from JSON Schemas in `docs/schemas/` (`npm run generate:contracts`) and checked by `verify:contracts`.

## How does Agent City use it?

1. City's data provider builds a `PluginRequestV1` with `method: "data.read"` and `payload: {projection: "city", version: 2, windowDays}`, then sends it through the host transport. With the developer switch `?cityData=v3` it reads `city:v3` page by page instead.
2. The host checks that the request came from City's active WebView, that `city:v2` is declared, and runs `query::app_local::city_projection` in Rust.
3. City validates the response with `validateCityProjectionV2` and maps each session to a building in `cityModel.ts`. See [City model](https://ohagent.ai/docs/architecture/city-model).
4. The Findings and Skills panels, and per-building details when v3 is on, call `city:v3` on demand.
5. In the browser (website demo, standalone preview), the same provider returns a synthetic fixture with `source: "fixture"` and never calls a host.

## What data interfaces can a plugin read?

| Projection | Method | What it returns | Who uses it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `harnesses:v1` | `harnesses.list` | Sources: opaque id, display name, capabilities | Any plugin that declares it |
| `harnesses:v1` | `harnesses.sessions` | Per-source session stats for a 7/30/90/366-day window, at most 500 sessions per source, no excerpts or cost | Any plugin that declares it |
| `city:v2` | `data.read` | City's view: up to 4,000 sessions with token split, model IDs, cost estimate and status, bounded titles and excerpts, plus window totals, models and daily activity | Plugins that declare it (only City today) |
| `city:v3` | `data.read` with `operation` | Paged City view on one data snapshot (see below) | City only (`plugin_id` check) |
| `city-settings:v1` | `data.read` | City's private seed setting | City only |

`harnesses:v1` is the general Agent Vitals interface. `city:v2` and `city:v3` are shaped for City. **TBD:** whether to promote a general, documented "Vitals data interface" that new apps can rely on. Today a new plugin gets `harnesses:v1` only, unless a new Rust projection handler is added.

Reads take a consistent snapshot. If the data changes between `harnesses.list` and `harnesses.sessions`, the host returns `revision_changed` and the SDK retries up to three times.

### What are the five `city:v3` operations?

Every `city:v3` request carries `operation`. The host accepts only these five, each with its own allowed fields:

| Operation | Extra fields | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `overview` | `windowDays`, `timezone`, `calendar_mode` (`rolling` only), `page_size` | Snapshot context, window, source identities, `overview` and `activity` modules, and the first page of sessions |
| `sessions.page` | `cursor`, `page_size` | The next page from the same snapshot |
| `session.detail` | `id`, `include_excerpts` | One session with its cost breakdown and excerpts |
| `module.read` | `module` (`findings` or `skills`), optional `harness` | One data module; `workflow` is reported as unsupported |
| `assets.resolve` | `save_id`, `asset_refs` | Whether saved City asset IDs still exist |

- **Pages:** default 200 sessions, at most 500. The window is half-open, `[from, to)`.
- **Snapshots:** every request after `overview` must send back `expected_revision` and `snapshot`. If the data changed in between, the host answers `revision_changed`. City then drops the pages it has collected and starts again, at most 3 times.

## What else can a plugin ask the host for?

- **Open a session in the workbench** (`navigationTargets: ["session"]`). The plugin sends its opaque handle; Rust resolves it and only returns `{opened: true}`.
- **Save a file** (`allowLocalExports: true`). The file is a blob download, and the user picks the destination in a native save dialog. No network downloads, no arbitrary file writes.
- **Private state keys** (`stateKeys`), for example City's `flight-profile:v1`.

## How do I add a new official plugin?

The repo's guide (`docs/OFFICIAL_PLUGIN_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md`) covers the full steps. In short:

1. Create the frontend at `apps/<name>/ui/` with a `build` script and a dependency on `@agent-vitals/app-sdk`. Commit the lockfile.
2. Add an entry to `apps/desktop/plugins.json` with `id`, `name`, `entry` (`plugins/<Name>.plugin/ui/index.html`), `commandNamespace`, `source` and `dataProjections`.
3. If it needs data beyond `harnesses:v1`, add a versioned Rust projection handler in `plugin_projections.rs`, backed by a query in `crates/agent-vitals-query`. Declaring a projection doesn't implement it.
4. Rebuild the desktop app. The registry is compiled in.

`id` can't clash with host tabs such as `overview`, `usage`, `sessions`, `findings`, `trust`, `skills` or `settings`.

## Can third parties publish plugins?

Not today. The desktop plugin host loads only the official UI plugins compiled into the app from `plugins.json`. There are no third-party native plugins and no dynamic install. Independent or externally installed apps would need package signing, process identity, sandboxing and per-request data grants. The repo has specs for these (`docs/APP_PACKAGE_SIGNATURE_CONTRACT_V1.md`, `docs/AGENT_VITALS_EXTENSION_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC.md`), but the policy says it doesn't certify their implementation. **TBD:** whether a third-party plugin path is on the roadmap.

## Related

- [Agent Vitals engine overview](https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/overview)
- [City model](https://ohagent.ai/docs/architecture/city-model)
- [Architecture overview](https://ohagent.ai/docs/architecture/overview)
- [Integrations overview](https://ohagent.ai/docs/integrations)

# Agent Vitals Python twin: the byte-for-byte compatible implementation
URL: https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/python

Next to the Rust engine, Agent Vitals keeps a Python implementation in `packages/agent-vitals-python/agent_vitals/`. It's a compatibility twin: for the same input, both must produce byte-identical output, which golden tests check in CI. It uses only the standard library, targets Python 3.9, and is what the ClawHub skill package runs through `scripts/scan.py`. The desktop app and Agent City use the Rust engine, not Python.

## Key facts

- **Location:** `packages/agent-vitals-python/agent_vitals/`, with `adapters/` (per agent), `agent/` (sessions, cost, usage facts, manifests, MCP) and `skills/` (skill audit).
- **Entry point:** `python3 scripts/scan.py …` (a thin wrapper that puts the package on the path).
- **Parity:** `python3 tests/golden_runner.py --diff` compares against `golden/`; with `AGENT_VITALS_BIN` set, it compares the Rust binary too.
- **Python version:** 3.9 in CI.
- **Not bundled** with the desktop app; manifest sources don't need Python either.

## Which commands does it have?

The Python CLI mirrors the skill-auditor and session-audit commands: `list`, `overlap`, `doctor`, `plan`, `explain`, `snapshot`, `diff`, `behavior`, `duration-audit`, `harnesses`, `codex-evidence`, `codex-session`, `sessions`, `oneline`, `calendar`, `state`, `budget`, plus `manifest-validate`. **TBD:** the complete list; some subcommands are registered without a simple `add_parser("name")` call and weren't counted here.

## Why keep two implementations?

The Python version came first and is the reference ("oracle") for output contracts. Keeping both in lockstep means a contract change shows up as a golden diff that has to be reviewed. Golden files must never be refreshed just to silence a failure.

## Related

- [Agent Vitals engine overview](https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/overview)
- [CLI](https://ohagent.ai/docs/vitals/cli)
- [Add a new data source](https://ohagent.ai/docs/contributing/adding-a-data-source)

# How is Oh Agent built? Architecture overview (Agent Vitals + Agent City)
URL: https://ohagent.ai/docs/architecture/overview

Oh Agent is an open-source platform for analyzing AI agent behavior data. Agents are now part of everyday work and life, and Oh Agent's goal is to make your agents' history useful to you. Oh Agent is built on the open-source Agent Vitals engine, and Agent City is its first app:

- **Agent Vitals**, the foundation: a local-first agent behavior data engine, embedded in the app (no server, no network port, no daemon). It finds the session logs your agents already write, parses them, and stores usage facts and behaviour findings in a local SQLite database. Then it serves that data through narrow, read-only interfaces.
- **Agent City**, built on top. It's an open-world data-visualization game that reads one of those interfaces and turns your sessions into a 3D city you can explore and replay.

Everything runs on your Mac. Nothing in this path uploads your data.

What "game" means today: desktop City has free flight and ring challenges, and driving is still in development. The web demo hides the game controls.

## Key facts

- **Desktop shell:** Tauri 2 (`tauri = "2"`), app `Oh Agent.app`, identifier `ai.ohagent.desktop`, version `1.0.0-beta.2`.
- **Workbench UI:** React 19 + Vite + Tailwind 4, in `apps/desktop/ui-dev/`.
- **Agent City:** React 19 + three.js 0.186 + Vite, TypeScript, in `apps/agent-city/ui/`.
- **Core:** a Rust workspace of layered crates under `crates/` (data, domain, harnesses, query, ingest, billing, trust, MCP).
- **CLI:** `agent-vitals` (`apps/cli/`). The desktop bundle ships it as `bin/agent-vitals`.
- **Storage:** one SQLite file, `agent-vitals.sqlite3`, in the data folder `~/.agent-vitals/` (override with `AGENT_VITALS_HOME`).
- **Website:** static landing page in `website/landing/`, plus a copy of the real City frontend that only gets synthetic data.
- **Naming:** the desktop app is `Oh Agent.app` (`ai.ohagent.desktop`, renamed on dev in `5c29146`). Crates, the CLI, the internal executable `agent-vitals-menubar` and the data folder still use `agent-vitals`.

## What are the two layers, in code?

| Layer | What it is | Where it lives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Agent Vitals: sources and parsing** | Per-agent log parsers and the source registry | `crates/agent-vitals-harnesses/` (`src/sources/session_harnesses.rs` is the registry) |
| **Agent Vitals: storage and sync** | Sync service, tick, watcher, SQLite authority database | `crates/agent-vitals-ingest/`, `crates/agent-vitals-data/` |
| **Agent Vitals: metrics** | Pure rules, cost and billing, diagnostics | `crates/agent-vitals-domain/`, `crates/agent-vitals-billing/`, `crates/vitals-core/` |
| **Agent Vitals: data interface** | Read-only projections for apps, the Data MCP server, the CLI and exports | `crates/agent-vitals-query/src/query/` (`app_harnesses.rs`, `app_local.rs`, `export.rs`), `crates/agent-vitals-mcp/`, `apps/cli/` |
| **Host bridge** | Checks which plugin may read which projection, then calls the query layer | `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/plugin_host.rs`, `plugin_projections.rs` |
| **Plugin protocol** | Shared TypeScript types and transport | `packages/agent-vitals-app-sdk/` (`harness-data.ts`, `city-ui-projection.ts`) |
| **Agent City** | Renderer, replay, flight and driving, photo and film export | `apps/agent-city/ui/`, registered in `apps/desktop/plugins.json` |

City reaches Vitals only through the host: `City → SDK plugin_request → PluginHost → plugin_projections → query::app_local → read-only database`. City never opens the database, never gets SQL, and never sees log paths.

How clean is the boundary? Partly clean.

- **Clean:** City has no Rust code and no database access. It only gets the projections declared in `plugins.json` (`city:v2`, `city:v3`, `city-settings:v1`, `harnesses:v1`). The generic `harnesses:v1` interface (`harnesses.list` / `harnesses.sessions`) is not City-specific.
- **Not yet clean (TBD):** City's main feed, `city:v2`, is a City-only projection. Its query (`app_local.rs`) and its type (`CityUiProjectionV2`) are both named for City and sit inside the shared Vitals query crate and SDK. `plugin_projections.rs` also hard-codes City (`if plugin_id != "city"`) for session navigation and for the newer paged `city:v3`, so on dev the special-casing has grown, not shrunk. A second app couldn't reuse `city:v2` as-is. Whether to generalize it into a public "Vitals data interface v1" is an open design question.
- **Not one package:** "Agent Vitals" is the whole Rust workspace plus the CLI, the Python twin and the desktop workbench. No single crate is called "Vitals" (`vitals-core` is only the diagnostics core). The desktop workbench reads Vitals data through its own Tauri IPC commands in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, not through the plugin interface.

## How do the parts fit together?

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Disk["Your Mac (read-only inputs)"]
    CC["~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl"]
    CX["~/.codex/sessions + archived_sessions<br/>rollout-*.jsonl"]
    DSH["$DSH_HOME or ~/.dsh/sessions"]
    WB["~/.workbuddy/traces"]
    MF["harnesses.d/&lt;slug&gt;/manifest.json<br/>(local manifest sources)"]
  end
  subgraph Core["Agent Vitals (crates/ + apps/cli)"]
    H["agent-vitals-harnesses<br/>parsers + source registry"]
    I["agent-vitals-ingest<br/>sync tick + watcher"]
    DB[("agent-vitals.sqlite3<br/>authority DB")]
    Q["agent-vitals-query<br/>read-only projections"]
    M["agent-vitals-mcp<br/>Data MCP tools"]
  end
  subgraph App["Desktop app (Tauri 2) + Agent City"]
    WBN["Workbench (React)"]
    PH["PluginHost"]
    CITY["Agent City plugin<br/>React + three.js"]
  end
  CC & CX & DSH & WB & MF --> H --> I --> DB
  DB --> Q --> PH --> CITY
  Q --> WBN
  DB --> M --> AG["Your local AI agent<br/>(stdio MCP client)"]
```

In words: agent log folders on disk (Agent Vitals inputs) → harness parsers → sync service → SQLite authority database → read-only query layer → either the desktop UI (workbench and the Agent City plugin) or the local Data MCP server.

## What are the Rust layers?

The core is split into crates that may only depend on lower layers. `agent-vitals-runtime` is a facade that re-exports them.

| Layer | Crate | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L0–L1 | `agent-vitals-runtime-core` | Data folder, clock, state files, pricing tables, logging |
| L2–L3 | `agent-vitals-query` | Source registry, session lookups, read-only queries and projections (including City's `app_local.rs`) |
| L4 | `agent-vitals-billing` | Budgets, price discovery, quota reminders |
| L5 | `agent-vitals-ingest` | Sync service, 5-minute tick, file watcher, findings evaluation, manifest install |
| L5 | `agent-vitals-trust` | Trust / egress audit |
| L6 | `agent-vitals-mcp` | Data MCP tools (the outbound face) |
| — | `agent-vitals-harnesses` | Per-agent log parsing (Claude Code, Codex, DSH, WorkBuddy, generic manifests) |
| — | `agent-vitals-domain`, `agent-vitals-data`, `vitals-core` | Pure rules, SQLite schema and writers, diagnostics core |

## Where does each part live in the repo?

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/desktop/src-tauri/` | Tauri host: tray, IPC commands, `plugin_host.rs`, `plugin_projections.rs` |
| `apps/desktop/ui-dev/` | React workbench (Overview, Usage, Sessions, Settings…) |
| `apps/desktop/plugins.json` | Registry of official built-in plugins (currently only City) |
| `apps/agent-city/ui/` | City renderer, replay, flight/driving, photo and film export |
| `packages/agent-vitals-app-sdk/` | Shared plugin protocol and UI transport |
| `apps/cli/` | `agent-vitals` CLI, including `data-mcp serve` |
| `crates/` | Rust core (table above) |
| `packages/agent-vitals-python/` | Python compatibility implementation, kept byte-identical via golden tests |
| `catalog/` | Official pricing catalog and (empty) source-manifest index |
| `integrations/dsh/` | DeepSeek Harness skill bundle |
| `website/landing/` | ohagent.ai landing page and synthetic City demo |

## How is it built and tested?

- **Rust:** `cargo test --release`, and `cargo clippy --release --all-targets -- -D warnings` as the CI lint gate. The desktop crate is its own workspace, so building the CLI does not build the app.
- **Python parity:** `python3 tests/golden_runner.py --diff` checks byte-for-byte golden outputs; the same runner can compare the Rust binary against Python.
- **City:** `npm --prefix apps/agent-city/ui run typecheck`, plus the `verify:city*` scripts in `apps/desktop/ui-dev/package.json`.
- **macOS app:** `bash scripts/build-macos-react-app.sh`, then open the `.app` bundle. Never run the bare menubar binary.
- **CI workflows** (`.github/workflows/`): `verify.yml`, `app-contracts.yml`, `desktop-platforms.yml` (Windows/Linux packages), `release.yml`, `release-desktop.yml`, `pricing-sync.yml` (daily at 03:17 UTC), `package-clawhub.yml`.

## What does the website run?

The landing page at ohagent.ai embeds a build of the real City frontend from `apps/agent-city/ui`, produced by `tools/build-city3d.mjs` into `website/landing/city3d/`. It only receives synthetic sessions and never reads local logs.

## Design rules worth knowing

- **Read, don't record.** Oh Agent installs no hooks or telemetry; it reads what agents already wrote.
- **No upload.** Network use is limited to public price/FX catalogs, release checks and explicitly chosen official downloads, with no local data in requests.
- **Raw text stays in the agents' logs.** The database stores anchors and counts, not full transcripts.
- **Honest numbers.** Unknown prices stay "unresolved", never zero.
- **Plugins never touch the database.** The host runs the query and returns only the declared projection.

## Roadmap / 规划中

Not in the code at `dev` `bf7196a`. Listed so readers don't mistake plans for features.

- **TBD:** Agents that help build your city through MCP. Today's Data MCP server reads usage data and offers typed settings actions; it has no tool that edits the city.
- **TBD:** Incremental hot update. City refreshes on its own after each sync, but it reloads the full projection and rebuilds the scene; sending only changed sessions and patching single buildings isn't implemented. See [Data pipeline](https://ohagent.ai/docs/architecture/data-pipeline#how-does-agent-city-update-when-new-sessions-arrive).
- **TBD:** A community gallery of cities (UGC). No code for this exists in the repo.
- **TBD:** Signed public installers. GitHub Releases is still empty.

See [Integrations](https://ohagent.ai/docs/integrations) for the full list of what exists today.

# How does Oh Agent turn agent session logs into data? The data pipeline
URL: https://ohagent.ai/docs/architecture/data-pipeline

Oh Agent's data pipeline has four steps: **discover** each agent's log files, **diff** them against what was already imported, **parse** new events into usage facts, and **write** those facts to a local SQLite database in one transaction. A sync runs every 5 minutes; on the desktop app, a file watcher can start it early when logs change.

## Key facts

- **Sources** come from one registry, in this order: `claude-code` → `codex` → `dsh` → `workbuddy`.
- **Only changed files are parsed.** Each file's size and modification time are remembered in a `source_files` table.
- **Every fact has a stable ID**, so re-importing a file creates duplicates that are dropped, not double counts.
- **One sync batch = one SQLite transaction**, so the database is never half-written.
- **Default sync interval:** 300 seconds. The file watcher wakes the sync about 1.2 seconds after a log changes (at most 5 seconds while it keeps growing); it never writes to the database itself.
- **City refreshes itself** after each sync that changes data, by reloading the full projection.
- **The database stores counts and anchors, not transcripts.** Raw text stays in the agents' own log files.

## Which folders are read?

| Source | Harness id | Files read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `claude-code` | `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` |
| Codex | `codex` | `~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl` and `~/.codex/archived_sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl` |
| DeepSeek Harness | `dsh` | `$DSH_HOME/sessions/**/session.jsonl` (or `.jsonl.zstd`); `DSH_HOME` defaults to `~/.dsh` |
| WorkBuddy | `workbuddy` | `trace_*.json` under `~/.workbuddy/traces/` |
| Local manifest sources | `harness:<slug>` | Whatever the manifest in `harnesses.d/<slug>/manifest.json` declares |

You can also add extra folders for Claude Code, Codex and DSH in Settings. See [Custom folders and manifest sources](https://ohagent.ai/docs/integrations/custom-sources-and-manifests).

## What happens in one sync?

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant T as Tick (every 5 min) / watcher
  participant S as sync_service
  participant H as Harness parsers
  participant DB as agent-vitals.sqlite3
  T->>S: run sync
  S->>H: list files for each registered source (+ custom folders)
  S->>DB: compare (size, mtime) in source_files
  S->>H: parse only new or changed files
  H-->>S: usage facts (tokens, model, time, session)
  S->>DB: one transaction: sync_runs, source_files, sessions, usage_facts
```

1. **Discover.** For each source in the registry, list its files under the default folder and under any custom folders you added.
2. **Diff.** Skip files whose size and modification time match the last import. A lost fingerprint only causes a re-parse; duplicates are dropped by fact ID.
3. **Parse.** The source's parser turns log lines into usage facts: input tokens (uncached, cache read, cache write), output tokens, model, timestamps and session.
4. **Write.** All facts of one batch, plus file fingerprints and session rows, are committed in a single immediate transaction.
5. **Enrich.** Session titles are read from side indexes where the agent keeps them, and behaviour findings are evaluated for Claude Code, Codex and DSH.

## How does Agent City update when new sessions arrive?

City refreshes on its own a few seconds after an agent writes to its log. It isn't an incremental, Vite-style hot patch yet: each refresh reloads the whole projection and rebuilds the city scene.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  W["File watcher<br/>(debounce 1.2 s, max 5 s)"] --> S["sync_service<br/>(one transaction)"]
  S --> R{"revision moved?"}
  R -- yes --> E["Invalidated event<br/>to the workbench"]
  E --> P["plugin_invalidate"]
  P --> C["City refetches<br/>full city:v2"]
  C --> B["Full scene rebuild<br/>stable layout, height animation"]
```

1. **Watch.** The file watcher waits 1.2 seconds after the last write, or at most 5 seconds while a log keeps growing, then wakes the sync. The 5-minute tick is the fallback.
2. **Sync.** New facts are committed in one transaction, which moves the database revision forward.
3. **Invalidate.** The desktop app emits one `Invalidated` event per new revision. A repeated revision is swallowed, so there's no time-based debounce here.
4. **Notify City.** The workbench calls `plugin_invalidate`, which fires `__AV_PLUGIN_INVALIDATED__` in City's WebView. A City tab that was hidden gets the same call when you switch back.
5. **Refetch.** City asks for the full `city:v2` projection again (up to 4,000 sessions). It doesn't fetch only the changed sessions.
6. **Rebuild.** If the data changed, City throws away the scene and builds it again. The previous layout is reused, so within one island tier existing buildings keep their lots. Buildings you already saw keep their height; new ones grow from the ground.

- **Opt-in paging:** with `?cityData=v3`, the same refresh reads `city:v3` page by page from one snapshot. A data change during loading restarts the read instead of mixing two versions.
- **Not implemented:** incremental diffs (only changed sessions) and patching single buildings. **TBD:** whether this is planned; see the [Roadmap](https://ohagent.ai/docs/integrations#roadmap--规划中).

## Where do session titles come from?

| Source | Title source |
| --- | --- |
| Codex | `~/.codex/session_index.jsonl` (`thread_name`) |
| Claude Code | the AI-generated title inside the session log |
| DSH | `<DSH_HOME>/storages/workspace.json` (workspace title) |
| WorkBuddy | not wired yet |

Titles are scrubbed and length-bounded before they reach the City view.

## How are costs kept honest?

Costs are estimated separately from the city. When the provider or route of a request can't be proven, usage is kept and marked as a **metered estimate** with `has_unresolved = true`, never silently dropped or counted as zero. City shows each session's estimated cost and its status (estimated, subscription, unpriced or unavailable), but cost never changes a building's height.

## What is never stored?

- Credentials and API keys. They are never written to anything Oh Agent owns.
- Full transcripts. The database keeps source anchors and short, scrubbed excerpts; full text is read from the original log only when you view it locally.
- If an agent deletes or rotates its log, Oh Agent shows that the source has expired instead of inventing data.

## Where is the data folder?

`~/.agent-vitals/` by default, or the folder in `AGENT_VITALS_HOME`. The database is `agent-vitals.sqlite3` inside it. Plugin state such as the City seed lives in `state/plugins/city.json`. Custom folders are listed in `state/custom-sources.json`.

**How long is data kept?** 13 months by default; you can set 1 to 60 months in Settings. **TBD:** confirm in the UI that pruning also removes old sessions from the City window (366 days fits inside the default).

## Related

- [Architecture overview](https://ohagent.ai/docs/architecture/overview)
- [City model: how sessions become buildings](https://ohagent.ai/docs/architecture/city-model)
- [Claude Code data source](https://ohagent.ai/docs/data-sources/claude-code) · [Codex data source](https://ohagent.ai/docs/data-sources/codex)
- [Add a new data source](https://ohagent.ai/docs/contributing/adding-a-data-source)
